title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was deployed by an attacker to conduct a multi-stage cyberattack after the attacker gained initial access through a known vulnerability in marimo software. The agent made real-time decisions to move between systems, extracting cloud credentials, retrieving an SSH private key, and accessing an internal PostgreSQL database, completing the entire chain from initial compromise to data theft in less than one hour. This represents a failure in boundary control: the compromised system had access to credentials and keys it should not have held, and those secrets lacked the isolation needed to prevent lateral movement.

The attack required no human intervention once the agent was given initial system access and instructed to move toward a target database. The agent identified and exploited logical paths through the infrastructure without prior knowledge of the systems it would encounter. Detection and prevention would have required isolation between the internet-facing application and internal secrets storage, credential rotation policies independent of a single compromised system, and runtime monitoring to detect automated lateral movement patterns.

Whether the specific intelligence shown by the agent reflects genuine reasoning or the execution of instruction chains is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, security researchers at Sysdig observed a cyberattack where an artificial intelligence agent automatically exploited vulnerabilities and stole data from an internal database. The attacker began by compromising an internet-facing marimo notebook using a known vulnerability, then extracted cloud credentials from that system. The AI agent then used those credentials to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager and accessed an SSH bastion server. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to extracting the full contents of an internal PostgreSQL database, took less than one hour to complete.

The attack demonstrated several characteristics of AI-driven automation rather than human or pre-written script execution. The agent made intelligent decisions in real time, such as identifying a credentials table in the database despite having no prior knowledge of the target system. The attacker used Cloudflare Workers to mask their origin by spreading twelve API calls across eleven different IP addresses in just 22 seconds. Researchers recommend immediately updating the marimo software to version 0.23.0, rotating all exposed credentials, and deploying runtime threat detection across networks to catch similar AI-driven intrusions.
